candidates.particulars: Name: Philip Grant Holladay. Age: 78. Gender: male. Nationality: American. Race/ethnicity: White, non-Hispanic, within the broad census-style category. Residence: Fort Collins, Colorado. Gross household income: over $200,000 annually, mainly from retirement benefits, investments, and his spouse’s consulting work. Partnership status: married to Mara for 49 years. Children status: neither has children. Political identification: moderately conservative; he values personal responsibility, continuity, and limited government, while accepting a role for public programs. Reading interest: he enjoys reading for leisure, especially engineering history, biographies, and books about the natural world.
candidates.life_course: Philip grew up in Ohio and studied civil engineering at a public university. He spent most of his career designing and overseeing municipal infrastructure projects, eventually managing a small technical team. Mara worked in education and later did independent consulting. They chose not to have children and built a life around work, friendships, and outdoor interests. He retired from full-time work several years ago but occasionally reviews technical documents for former colleagues. Their income is comfortable, though they still make deliberate decisions about investment risk and large purchases.
candidates.daily_life: He starts mornings with coffee, a newspaper, and a chapter of whatever he is reading. He and Mara take regular walks, often meeting another couple for lunch or inviting friends over for a simple dinner. He helps with a local trail-maintenance group when the work suits his schedule, and enjoys repairing household items rather than replacing them. He keeps a few standing appointments but dislikes having every day planned in advance.
candidates.travel: Philip likes trips that combine scenery with a reason to stop and learn something: a national park, an engineering landmark, or a small town with a good local museum. He and Mara usually travel together by car, staying in comfortable inns or cabins and keeping driving days moderate. Their finances allow them to travel without pinching every expense, but he prefers spending on a memorable place or meal over conspicuous luxury. They have enough flexibility to take trips outside the busiest periods, while still planning around Mara’s occasional consulting commitments. On a past road trip through the Southwest, he shortened one driving leg after realizing they would enjoy the stops more than the mileage; he remembers that as a better choice than sticking to the original itinerary. He would like another scenic, unhurried trip, but has not committed to a destination.
candidates.personality_and_voice: Philip is measured and practical, and tends to ask how a plan will work in ordinary conditions. He often listens before giving an opinion, then explains his reasoning in a few concrete points. He can be quietly funny, especially about his own overplanning, and is more comfortable with a candid conversation than a sales pitch. He is not rigid about changing his mind when new information is useful.

candidates.particulars: Name: Philip Grant Holladay. Age: 84. Gender: male. Nationality: American. Race/ethnicity: White, non-Hispanic, within the broad census-style category. Residence: Cheyenne, Wyoming. Gross household income: at least $200,000 annually, supported by retirement income, investment income, and proceeds from the sale of his former business. Partnership status: married to Elaine, his spouse of 56 years. Children status: they have no children. Political identification: moderately conservative, with an emphasis on tradition, self-reliance, and limits on government, alongside acceptance of some public services. Reading interest: he reads for enjoyment and personal interest, particularly American history, courtroom accounts, and literary fiction.
candidates.life_course: Philip studied accounting and worked first in commercial lending before buying into an insurance brokerage with a longtime colleague. He ran the business for decades, sold his share before retirement, and remained in touch with several former employees. Elaine was a librarian and still has her own interests and friendships. They never had children; their closest family ties are with siblings, nieces, nephews, and old friends. Their accumulated savings and ongoing income give them room for travel, though Philip remains attentive to how a major expense fits into their long-term plans.
candidates.daily_life: He reads after breakfast, checks in with a few friends by phone, and keeps a modest schedule of errands and appointments. He and Elaine attend occasional concerts and community events, but prefer smaller gatherings where they can talk. Philip likes cooking a meal with Elaine on weekends and is the person who usually remembers to call relatives on birthdays. He follows local and national news, but does not want politics to dominate conversation.
candidates.travel: Philip is drawn to places with history, architecture, and a strong sense of local life rather than trips built around constant activity. He and Elaine might choose a guided city stay, a train journey, or a few days near a historic district, with comfortable lodging and time to rest between outings. Their finances make such travel feasible, and retirement gives them flexibility, though he likes to keep the itinerary clear and avoid unnecessarily tight connections. He would rather pay for a knowledgeable guide or a convenient room than add several stops to the schedule. On a past visit to the East Coast, he and Elaine abandoned a planned extra excursion in favor of an unhurried afternoon at a museum and dinner with friends; he still recalls the conversation more vividly than the missed attraction. He is interested in another history-focused trip, but the destination and timing remain open.
candidates.personality_and_voice: Philip is courteous, deliberate, and mildly formal with people he has just met. He enjoys comparing how institutions have changed over time and will sometimes offer a dry one-line observation after listening to a discussion. He likes having practical details settled, but does not need every hour accounted for. When asked what he thinks, he tends to distinguish between what he knows and what he is only guessing.

candidates.particulars: Name: Philip Grant Holladay. Age: 75. Gender: male. Nationality: American. Race/ethnicity: White, non-Hispanic, within the broad census-style category. Residence: Boise, Idaho. Gross household income: more than $200,000 annually, from his retirement income, investment distributions, and his spouse’s part-time professional work. Partnership status: married to Lucia for 34 years. Children status: they have no children. Political identification: moderately conservative; he favors personal responsibility and restrained government, while recognizing that some public programs are important. Reading interest: he enjoys reading for pleasure, especially travel writing, novels, and books about food and regional culture.
candidates.life_course: Philip was raised in the Pacific Northwest and trained as a physician. He practiced in a group clinic for many years, with a focus on long-term patient relationships, then shifted to part-time work before retiring. Lucia worked in publishing and now does occasional editorial projects from home. They have no children and have organized their lives around shared meals, a circle of friends, and travel. Their income is secure, but Philip still thinks carefully about how much of their time a commitment will consume, not only what it costs.
candidates.daily_life: He walks most mornings, often stopping for coffee, and spends part of the day reading or handling practical household tasks. He and Lucia cook together several nights a week and like inviting friends to try a dish they encountered on a trip. Philip belongs to a neighborhood book group where he is as interested in hearing other interpretations as in defending his own. He keeps in touch with former colleagues but no longer wants a calendar full of professional obligations.
candidates.travel: Philip and Lucia enjoy travel that lets them eat well, walk through neighborhoods, and understand how daily life differs from home. They prefer a small number of bases rather than changing hotels constantly, and are happy to mix independent days with a guided outing when it adds context. They have the time and resources for international travel, although Lucia’s occasional editorial deadlines and their preference for a manageable pace shape when they go. They choose comfortable, well-located lodging, not necessarily the most expensive option. On a previous trip to Portugal, Philip had arranged several restaurant reservations, but they ended up spending an evening at a neighborhood place recommended by someone they met; the spontaneous meal became one of his favorite memories. He would welcome another food-and-culture trip, while leaving the destination and details undecided.
candidates.personality_and_voice: Philip is sociable without needing to be the center of attention. He asks follow-up questions and remembers small details people have mentioned, especially about places they have lived or foods they enjoy. He can be decisive about practical matters but is willing to let a day unfold when there is no reason to hurry. His humor is warm and lightly self-deprecating, and he tends to describe an experience through a specific person, meal, or conversation.

candidates.particulars: Name: Philip Grant Holladay. Age: 89. Gender: male. Nationality: American. Race/ethnicity: White, non-Hispanic, within the broad census-style category. Residence: Missoula, Montana. Gross household income: over $200,000 annually, combining his retirement and investment income with his long-term partner’s retirement income. Partnership status: in a committed relationship with his girlfriend, Ruth; they share a household. Children status: neither has children. Political identification: moderately conservative, valuing tradition and individual responsibility while accepting some public programs. Reading interest: he enjoys leisure reading, particularly western history, mysteries, and memoirs.
candidates.life_course: Philip studied business administration and spent his working life as a financial controller for a regional manufacturing company. After retiring, he continued to help a few acquaintances with bookkeeping questions but never returned to regular employment. He was widowed before meeting Ruth, a friend he had known socially for years; their relationship gradually became a shared household. Neither has children. Their income is substantial, largely because of years of saving and investment, and they use it to maintain a comfortable home and stay connected with friends and extended family.
candidates.daily_life: Philip likes a settled morning routine: breakfast, a few pages of a book, and a look at the news. He and Ruth take walks when the weather and their plans allow, and they often have a neighbor or old friend over for coffee. He enjoys small repair projects and keeps notes about family stories and places he has visited. They attend occasional local performances and make regular calls to nieces, nephews, and longtime friends, without treating every social invitation as an obligation.
candidates.travel: Philip prefers trips with familiar comforts and a clear purpose, such as visiting friends, seeing a historic site, or spending several quiet days in a scenic area. He and Ruth generally travel together, sometimes coordinating with friends, and choose a relaxed pace with convenient lodging and room for breaks. They can afford to travel and have flexibility, but Philip does not enjoy complicated itineraries or changing plans at the last minute. He is comfortable driving when the route is straightforward and would also consider a guided option if it reduces logistical work. On a past trip to visit friends, they dropped a planned second stop after enjoying an extended visit; Philip was glad they chose time with people over checking off another place. He would like to keep traveling, but any next trip will depend on what feels enjoyable and manageable to both of them.
candidates.personality_and_voice: Philip is steady and observant, with a preference for familiar routines but little need to impose them on other people. He speaks plainly and often pauses to find the detail he wants rather than reaching for a quick answer. He appreciates good organization, but can be persuaded by a personal recommendation. Around people he trusts, he tells gently comic stories about past miscalculations and is generous with his attention.
